reports.desc: I saw their ad on Facebook and thought the jacket was nice and I ordered it.  It came and doesn't fit and is of poor quality.  So I tried to send them an email (support@abrilene.com) about this and they won't respond back to me.  I want to return it but there was no contact information for them.  I had an address in Orlando, FL - 1234 Lakeview Ave., Suite 200, Orlando, FL 32801.  It was on their website and they won't respond to me.  My husband took the package to the post office and the address wasn't good.  I wanted to report this to warn others about them.

This business left a voicemail with an account number to call 877-870-8367.  I called them back and gave them my bank information.  My bank told me that this was a scam and they could not close my account.  I wanted to report this to the BBB to warn others.

I received multiple text messages claiming I had won a prize from “MrBeast.” The scammer pretended to be MrBeast and said I needed to contact an “assistant” to claim the prize. The messages came from several different phone numbers, including (562) 384-0857, (248) 342-4286, (252) 499-5375, (510) 776-xxxx, and +1 (716) 936-0969.The scammer tried to convince me to respond and follow instructions to claim a prize, which is a common impersonation scam. They attempted to get money or personal information by pretending to be a well-known public figure. I did not lose any money and did not provide any personal information. I am reporting this to help prevent others from falling for the same impersonation scam.

Scammer reached out to me about a job I never applied to. They sent fake offer letters via email, reached out on Google Chat, and promised a remote position, 30 days of PTO, and reimbursement for work equipment.
The tracker said items delivered. From date of order it took 23 days and I never received the merchandise.
Attachment is the fake offer letter sent to my email.

Jeffy Ramos, "ID":AMX110589 called and said a card was issued in my name, on 6/30/26, with an address in NYC associated, while I live in Chicago and hadn't been to NYC in 15 months. She said it was used to purchase pistols and ammo.  If I didn't report the identity theft within 2 hours my name would be reported to Homeland Security.  If I reported it to NYPD, which she "connected" me to, my name would be removed and my involvement would end.
Item not as described. Very small instead of picture shown
Did not pay back loan agreement and I won a lawsuit against defendant but have not been able to reclaim lost money.

It was offered a job to handmade different products . But after they started a tasks requirement to send the package of parts to put together as handmade products. Initially small amounts ( 10$ ) paired for tasks done . After they did change in prepaid tasks asking for 27$ , 30, 81 , 98, 130, 390, … increasing reach time . When I tried to withdraw the amount from the company account they said my score with company is only 96 and to get at 100 I have to pay 400x4 =1600$ more to be able to withdraw. I realized finally is a tasks scam and closed my account in chime used to make transactions for them. Closed my telegram account even it was my way to communicate with my family in Germany . Do not trust any offer for handmade jobs ! All are task scam , now !
I have received multiple threatening texts from AE Home Warranty notifying me of a closure; they have my cell phone and text nearly every day to respond or call.

A Middle Aged African American Gentleman that allegedly goes by the name Terrance Jacobs was doing.  door to door sales. The man sold me a $40 bottle of cleaning agent. Claims that it works on everything and bio-safe. etc. but the sale also supports the Youth in Chicago against gang violence. The man was nice, funny and a bit pushy. I bought so he would leave and to do a feel good thing. But after leaving. i immediately searched the info on the bottle and lead me to other people feeling scammed by the same service in the area. This incident occurred in Rockford IL, but they claimed to out from chicago. This appears to be a scam on selling over priced cleaners to support a seemingly non existent charity.
The Cleaning product they are selling is called " Get Gone ".
